quotes: Participants were allocated 1:1 to oral finerenone (10 mg or 20 mg once daily) or placebo. The main efficacy endpoints were: (i) a cardiovascular composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or hospitalisation for heart failure; and (ii) a kidney composite of kidney failure, a sustained ≥57% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from baseline over at least four weeks, or renal death. Analyses employed stratified Cox proportional-hazards models. **Results.** After excluding patients with critical Good Clinical Practice violations, 13 026 individuals were included (median follow-up 3.0 years; interquartile range 2.3–3.8).

quotes: Patients Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with type 2 diabetes and CKD treated with a maximum tolerated labelled dose of an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor (ACEi) or angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB). Chronic kidney disease in FIDELIO-DKD CKD in FIDELIO-DKD was defined as either: (i) persistent (demonstrated at both the run-in and screening visits, which took place between a minimum of 4 to a maximum of 16 weeks apart), moderately increased albuminuria (UACR ≥30–<300 mg/g) with an eGFR of ≥25–<60 mL/min/1.73 m 2 and the presence of diabetic retinopathy, or (ii) persistent, severely increased albuminuria (UACR ≥300–≤5000 mg/g) and an eGFR of ≥25–<75 mL/min/1.73 m 2 .

quotes: Procedures The procedures for the FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD studies have been described previously. Briefly, eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to receive oral finerenone (10 or 20 mg) or placebo. Both studies consisted of run-in, screening, double-blind treatment, and safety follow-up periods ( Supplementary material online , Figure S2 ). 7 , 10 The run-in period required ACEi or ARB therapy to be adjusted to a maximum tolerated labelled dose that did not lead to unacceptable side effects. Study drug was withheld if potassium concentrations exceeded 5.5 mmol/L and restarted when potassium levels fell to ≤5.0 mmol/L.

quotes: After prospective exclusion of 145 patients for critical GCP violations, the final analysis set comprised 13 026 participants (finerenone: 6519; placebo: 6507). ### Baseline Characteristics Demographic and clinical features were well balanced between treatment arms. The mean age was 64.8 years (SD 9.5); 69.8% were male. The population was predominantly White (68.1%), with 22.2% Asian and 4.0% Black/African American. Mean glycated haemoglobin was 7.7% (SD 1.4) and mean systolic blood pressure 136.7 mmHg (SD 14.2). Mean eGFR was 57.6 mL/min/1.73 m² (SD 21.7), and median UACR was 515 mg/g (interquartile range 198–1147); 66.7% of patients had severely increased albuminuria (UACR ≥300 mg/g).
